title: Education unions call for strike in Catalonia

tea.why: Unions are protesting to demand increased teaching staff, better inclusive education resources, lower student-teacher ratios, and salary changes.
tea.want: Increased teaching staff, more inclusive education resources, reduced student-teacher ratios, and improved salary conditions.
tea.changed: Nov 25: The union Ustec filed a legal challenge with the TSJC to suspend the government-mandated minimum service requirements for the strike.

summary: Education unions including Ustec, CGT, COS, and La Intersindical have called for a strike across Catalonia on November 26, 2026. The action follows a decision by the Asamblea Educativa de Catalunya to push for improved working conditions, including higher staffing levels and reduced student-teacher ratios. The Catalan government's Department of Business and Labor has established minimum service requirements, mandating that schools maintain specific staffing levels for teaching, dining, and extracurricular activities to ensure student safety. The union Ustec has criticized these requirements as excessive, noting they are stricter than those applied during a general strike on November 11. Consequently, the union has appealed to the High Court of Justice of Catalonia to suspend the government's minimum service order, arguing it infringes upon the fundamental right to strike.
response: The Department of Business and Labor established minimum service requirements for the strike, mandating specific staffing levels for teaching and support services to ensure student safety and care.

updates.text: The Department of Business and Labor set minimum service requirements for the upcoming November 26 strike.
The union Ustec filed a legal challenge with the TSJC to contest the minimum service requirements.
